newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt state offers stake in joint bank.
newsitem.headline: Egypt state offers stake in joint bank.

text.p: The Egyptian state offered private investors on Friday an initial 20,400 share tranche of its stake in joint venture Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank.

The state-owned National Investment Bank said in a published advertisement it would sell the tranche, which represents 1.8 percent of Alexandria Commercial and Maritime's total 1.125 million shares, at the highest bid price and set a floor of 140 pounds ($41.2) per share.

Alexandria Commercial and Martime rarely-traded shares are denominated in U.S. dollars and Egyptian pounds. The stock closed on Thursday 6.5 pounds higher at 130.28 pounds. The dollar shares last traded on March 16.
The advertisement said investors can buy a minimum 100 shares and the offer will open on Monday April 7 and close the following day.
Shareholders will be entitled to the 1996 dividend, which has yet to be decided by the bank's board, it said.
State owned firms and banks own a large tranche of Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank. The shareholders include the Bank of Alexandria, Misr Insurance and Public Holding for Shipping.
The privatisation is in line with the goverment's programme to get out of joint-venture banks. The state is also considering privatising one of its major retail banks.
The advertisement showed that Alexandria Commercial and Maritime Bank made unaudited net pre-tax profits of 35.4 million pounds in calendar 1996 compared to 16.8 million in the previous year.
The bank's assets rose to 1.09 billion in 1996 from 925.8 million in 1995. Customer deposits were also higher in 1996 at 790 million from 679.9 million in the previous year.
